doc.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025

title: Starting on guitar, then string bass
summary: He began on guitar through his dad, wanted drums, and took up bass in junior high after his sister's Stan Getz record.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You started as a guitar player, right?

I started playing as a guitar player because of my dad, yeah. I wanted to be a drummer but I lived in a second story apartment and that wasn’t going to happen. As a matter of fact when I got a set of drums I put them in the basement and there was a gigantic fight so I had to get rid of them. And I tried rock bands in the cellar and everything and it didn’t work out with my family so I had to get them out of there and find another place for them. But, so yeah I played a little guitar, I took some lessons, and in junior high I started with string bass ‘cause of my sister’s love for a Stan Getz record which had Astrud Gilberto on it, “The Girl from Ipanema.” And she loved that record. And on the flip side of that record I remember was Stan’s group swinging. And one of the songs the bassist starts off the tune playing the bass line for a blues, I think it was a blues. And I loved it. So when I got to junior high and I was able to get ahold of a string bass I went right for it. And of course I had known the guitar a little bit, it was easy for me to get in there except for the large intervals and big strings.
